Rank models by AIC or AICc

Source: R/aic_tab.R
aic_tab.Rd

Build a model-selection table ranked by AICc (the default) or AIC for a list of fitted models. Each estimated scale of effect (sigma), and each estimated kernel shape, counts as a parameter, so a scale-optimized model competes fairly with fixed-scale or non-spatial alternatives in the same list. Lists can mix multiScaleR objects with plain fitted models such as glm objects.

vignette("v02-user-guide", package = "multiScaleR") compares kernels and model structures with these tables, including an N-mixture model.

Usage

aic_tab(mod_list,
        AICc = TRUE,
        mod_names = NULL,
        verbose = FALSE,
        ...)

Arguments

mod_list

A list of fitted models: multiScaleR objects from multiScale_optim(), plain fitted models (for example glm or lm), or both. Every model must be fitted to the same observations with a comparable likelihood (see "Check that models are comparable"). Bayesian fits, cross-validation results, and private spatial prototypes are rejected.

AICc

Logical. If TRUE (the default), rank by the second-order corrected AIC (AICc). Set FALSE for standard AIC. AICc is recommended when the number of observations is small relative to the number of parameters (n / K < 40 is a common rule of thumb). AICc requires n > K + 1 for every model and raises an error otherwise. Use AICc = FALSE in that case.

mod_names

Optional character vector of model names, one per model in mod_list. By default, multiScaleR objects are labeled [kernel=...; family=...] followed by the right-hand side of the model formula. unmarked labels name the model class and, where present, the mixture, so Poisson, negative binomial, and ZIP alternatives get distinct labels.

verbose

Logical. If TRUE, the table is also printed to the console. Default FALSE.

...

Not used.

Value

A data frame of class "aictab" (from the AICcmodavg package), sorted from the best (smallest) criterion value, with one row per model:

  • Modnames: model name, from mod_names or the default label.

  • K: number of estimated parameters. It counts the fitted likelihood parameters, including ancillary ones such as negative binomial dispersion (or native effective degrees of freedom for GAMs), plus each estimated scale and shape of a multiScaleR model.

  • AICc or AIC: the information criterion. Smaller is better.

  • Delta_AICc or Delta_AIC: difference from the best model. Models within about 2 units of the best are generally considered to have comparable support.

  • ModelLik: relative likelihood of the model, exp(-0.5 * Delta).

  • AICcWt or AICWt: Akaike weight, the relative support for each model within this set. Weights sum to 1.

  • LL: maximized log-likelihood.

  • Cum.Wt: cumulative Akaike weight.

When a likelihood was adjusted (see "Count parameters"), the table carries a likelihood_adjustments attribute.

Count parameters

For a multiScaleR object, the log-likelihood and parameter count come from the refit model in opt_mod, and each estimated sigma (and shape, for kernel = "expow") is added to K. The AIC printed by the native model in opt_mod leaves those parameters out. Hard-radius metrics in an "expow" model add their estimated radius but no shape, and fixed-radius metrics add neither. Plain models in the list get no sigma. Otherwise the native log-likelihood degrees of freedom are used when available, so negative binomial dispersion counts as one parameter. Missing or inconsistent parameter metadata and non-finite log-likelihoods raise an error rather than guessing from predictor names.

  • unmarked models. The native AIC and log-likelihood determine the count. It includes every abundance or occupancy coefficient, every detection coefficient, factor contrasts, mixture parameters, and estimated random-effect standard deviations. Optimizer and TMB free-parameter metadata are checked for agreement when present. Latent abundances and realized random effects add nothing. For example, four abundance coefficients, three detection coefficients, and one random-effect standard deviation give eight native parameters, or nine with one estimated Gaussian scale. A table of fixed coefficients can therefore show fewer parameters than the fitted count.

  • The K argument of unmarked::pcount() is an upper bound for the abundance sum in the likelihood, not a parameter count. Check that the log-likelihood does not change when you refit with a larger bound.

  • spaMM HLfit models. spaMM::DoF() supplies the full count, including estimated residual, covariance, and correlation parameters. Realized random effects are not counted. The native default log-likelihood target is kept (p_v for ordinary maximum likelihood, p_bv for REML), so absolute REML criteria can differ from spaMM's marginal AIC, which uses p_v.

  • mgcv negative binomial BAMs. The table checks the native fit against the normalized count likelihood. A retained outer scale flag can otherwise add one to both the reported log-likelihood and the parameter count, even though the family scale is one. Verified fits use the normalized likelihood and native effective degrees of freedom plus an estimated theta, with no extra scale parameter. A fixed theta adds no parameter. The likelihood_adjustments attribute records the native and used likelihoods and regression-model counts for the affected models, before the scale and shape parameters are added. With large case weights, verification checks the native AIC arithmetic and a rescaled response-density comparison at the original tolerance, and records that method. Reported likelihoods keep the original weights. Unknown inconsistencies raise an error, and fitted coefficients, covariance, and diagnostics are unchanged.

Check that models are comparable

Information criteria compare models only when they describe the same observations with comparable likelihoods. The table checks the number of observations and, when native metadata can be recovered, the used row IDs, response values, binomial trials, likelihood weights, and the likelihood's response measure. Zero-weight GLM rows and removed unmarked sites are excluded from the used observations. Binomial counts and proportions with their trial weights are compared on the same count scale, and logical FALSE/TRUE outcomes, including success and failure columns, compare as 0 and 1 when trial totals and weights agree. Fitted responses, covariance, and parameter counts are not changed.

  • N-mixture models. Mixed unmarked::pcount() models keep their native marginal likelihood. Two models can share sites and the original count matrix yet use different visits when a detection covariate has missing values. The table recovers the visits each model used from its component formulas, including formula-specific missing observations and omitted sites, and stops when they differ. Equal count matrices and site totals alone do not establish comparability, and missing or inconsistent used-response metadata raises an error without falling back on raw data. Null abundance models and detection-only models without site covariates keep the native site count and their original response-row identities.

  • Distance-removal models. gdistremoval() comparisons check both distance and removal histories and their stored survey protocol, including the primary-period layout, distance bins and units, and removal durations. Equal paired totals are not enough. Distances in meters and kilometers are converted to meters in the comparison copy, and the fitted objects keep their native units. Harmonize time units and event definitions before comparing, because a native frame does not store a removal-time unit. Mixture and distance-key alternatives may share the same observed target. Check sensitivity to the integration cutoff separately.

  • Maximum likelihood and REML. ML and REML fits cannot be mixed, and REML comparisons require the same recoverable fixed-effect design.

  • Cox and conditional logistic models. Partial-likelihood comparisons require matching methods and equivalent stratum partitions.

These checks cannot certify metadata that a native provider does not store. You still need to establish that the likelihoods are scientifically comparable.

Sample size for AICc and BIC

  • unmarked models. AICc and BIC use the retained site rows, not visits or random-effect realizations. When groups repeat across rows, this convention does not establish a valid small-sample correction or an effective independent sample size.

  • Cox and conditional logistic models. AICc and BIC use the event count from the native log-likelihood metadata, so each supported choice set with one used step contributes one event, while every alternative row is still checked for comparability. This follows the native survival BIC convention. It does not adjust for dependence among steps or animals or establish that AICc is valid for a particular sampling design. Missing event-count metadata raises an error.

A finite criterion and an optimizer code of zero do not establish convergence, identifiability, or interval calibration. Read the native fit diagnostics, including the gradient and curvature when available.

Models the table rejects

  • Bayesian fits from multiScale_bayes(). A posterior mode or penalized target is not a maximized sampling likelihood for AIC or BIC. Posterior predictive comparison needs a separate workflow with its own target and diagnostics.

  • Cross-validation results, which hold held-out scores rather than a maximized likelihood. Use cv_tab() or select_cv().

  • Private spatial prototypes, which have no qualified maximized marginal likelihood. Conditional response densities and posterior objectives are not substitutes.

  • gdistremoval() models with active formula offsets or TMB zero inflation. These are rejected before fitting, model selection, or prediction. In the audited unmarked 1.5.2 provider, offsets did not enter the fitted likelihood, and the TMB ZIP likelihood ignored its zero-inflation parameter. These combinations need separate provider qualification. multiScaleR does not remove offsets, switch engines, alter parameter counts, or substitute uncertainty estimates. Offset-free C-engine ZIP models keep their native likelihood and parameter count.

The table itself is built with AICcmodavg::aictabCustom().

See also

bic_tab(), multiScale_optim(), cv_tab() for comparisons by held-out prediction, and vignette("v08-cross-validation", package = "multiScaleR").

Author

Bill Peterman

Examples

## Bundled counts simulated with a habitat scale of 75 map units
data("pts")
data("count_data")
hab <- terra::rast(system.file("extdata", "hab.tif", package = "multiScaleR"))
prepared <- kernel_prep(pts, hab, max_D = 300, sigma = 75, verbose = FALSE)
dat <- data.frame(y = count_data$y, prepared$kernel_dat)
fixed_model <- glm(y ~ hab, family = poisson(), data = dat)
null_model <- glm(y ~ 1, family = poisson(), data = dat)
spatial_model <- multiScale_optim(fixed_model, prepared, par = 75 / 300,
                                  n_cores = 1, verbose = FALSE)
models <- list(spatial = spatial_model, fixed = fixed_model, null = null_model)

## The fixed model already uses the true 75-unit scale, so the spatial model
## reaches the same log-likelihood and pays for one extra parameter (sigma).
aic_tab(models, AICc = FALSE, mod_names = names(models))
#> 
#> Model selection based on AIC:
#> 
#>         K    AIC Delta_AIC AICWt Cum.Wt      LL
#> fixed   2 232.34      0.00  0.73   0.73 -114.17
#> spatial 3 234.33      1.99  0.27   1.00 -114.17
#> null    1 346.69    114.35  0.00   1.00 -172.34
#> 
aic_tab(models, AICc = TRUE, mod_names = names(models))
#> 
#> Model selection based on AICc:
#> 
#>         K   AICc Delta_AICc AICcWt Cum.Wt      LL
#> fixed   2 232.51       0.00   0.75   0.75 -114.17
#> spatial 3 234.67       2.16   0.25   1.00 -114.17
#> null    1 346.74     114.23   0.00   1.00 -172.34
#> 

## K for a stored N-mixture fit: three abundance coefficients, one
## detection coefficient, and two estimated scales
nmix <- readRDS(system.file("extdata", "cache-user-guide-nmix.rds",
                            package = "multiScaleR"))
aic_tab(list(nmix), mod_names = "bin1 + cont2")
#> 
#> Model selection based on AICc:
#> 
#>              K    AICc Delta_AICc AICcWt Cum.Wt      LL
#> bin1 + cont2 6 1001.89          0      1      1 -494.33
#>
